$comment: ONE source of truth for the agent-reliability policy, next to mcp/registry.json.
Read by pi-extensions/reliability-core.ts (the live guard) and by tools/reliability.py
(the CLI, the MCP-server helper and the tests). Two readers, one file - a threshold
changed here changes both, and tests/reliability_parity.mjs proves they agree.
Why a file and not constants in code: the numbers below were measured against a 9B
Q4_K_M on 8 GB VRAM (12288-token response ceiling, ~17 KiB/token KV). They are the
tuning surface, and tuning a guard should not be a code edit in two languages.
Every value is deliberately conservative. A guard that blocks legitimate work is worse
than no guard, because the model then spends its turn arguing with the runtime.

loop_guard.$comment: Only FAILED calls are counted. A read that succeeds never increments anything, so polling and paginated search are untouched.
loop_guard.$comment_max_identical_failures: 1 = the FIRST identical retry after a hard failure is blocked. A hard failure (NOT_FOUND, PERMISSION_DENIED, INVALID_ARGUMENT) cannot become a success by repeating it unchanged.
loop_guard.$comment_max_identical_failures_transien: TIMEOUT / SERVER_UNAVAILABLE / OUTPUT_TOO_LARGE can be transient, so they get a bounded retry instead of an immediate block.
loop_guard.$comment_cycle: A -> B -> A -> B, all four failing with the same error codes, is a cycle: neither call is making progress and the pair will repeat forever.
loop_guard.$comment_memory: Session-scoped and capped. A 9B session issues tens of calls, not thousands; the cap only bounds a pathological run.

duplicate_success.$comment: An identical MUTATING call that already succeeded in the current generation is refused. The generation counter advances on every successful mutating call, so `edit file` then `build` then `edit file` then `build` is allowed - only a true repeat with no intervening change is not.
duplicate_success.$comment_tools: Only the two tools where a repeat is pointless. `bash` is NOT here: re-running a build or a test after reading its output is a normal, deliberate step, and blocking it would be the guard inventing a rule the agent cannot see.
duplicate_success.$comment_generation_tools: Any of these succeeding moves the world on: a recorded duplicate stops being a duplicate, and a previously failed call may now legitimately work.

$comment: The loop guard catches the SAME call repeated. It cannot catch a model that inspects
forty different things and writes nothing - every call is new, so no fingerprint
repeats. That was measured live: ornith-1.5-9b-uncensored on the moon-exploration
brief made 46 consecutive `bash` inspection calls in 12 minutes and created zero
files, re-reading the same files with different line ranges.
So the signal is not repetition, it is the absence of any mutation. A session with
N inspections and no write at all is not doing reconnaissance, it is circling.
Deliberately conservative: it only fires when NOTHING has been written yet, so an
agent that has already produced a file is never interrupted mid-edit.
$comment_mutations: Which tools count as 'the world changed'. Only tools that write a file belong here,
and only when the call succeeded. Everything that is neither an inspection nor a
write is NEUTRAL: it does not count as looking, it does not count as doing.
This list used to be implicit - 'anything that is not an inspection is a mutation' -
and that was wrong in a way a live run made obvious. `node --version` and
`python tool.py --help` are not inspections by prefix, so they were scored as
mutations, which set require_zero_mutations loose and disarmed the guard for the
whole session. The model then did 23 inspections with nothing written and was never
asked to stop. A guard that a harmless version check can switch off is not a guard.
`bash` is deliberately NOT here: a shell command may write (npm install, mkdir) or
may only look, and this layer cannot tell which without observing the disk. Rather
than guess in either direction it stays neutral - the guard keeps counting.
progress_guard.$comment_bash: `bash` is both a tool and a shell, so it is classified by the command it runs, not by its name. A prefix match on the first word (after stripping cd/&&/echo noise) is enough: `sed -n '1,60p' file` is inspection, `npm install` is not.

write_guard.$comment: Mirrors pi-extensions/write-guard.ts, which still owns the block. Kept here so the Python side can report the same budget and the tests can assert the two agree.

write_verification.$comment: A write/edit result is only reported as success when the file on disk actually changed. pi's write tool cannot lie, but a truncated generation or a redirected path can, and a 9B model will happily believe its own summary.

path_guard.$comment: block_outside_repo: a mutating call whose target resolves outside the repository root is refused - that is a sandbox escape, not a project choice. warn_outside_project: inside the repo but outside the active project is allowed (tools/, docs/, the repo root itself are legitimate) and only logged.

logging.$comment: JSONL, one event per line, no file contents, no prompts, no secrets. Rotated by tools/reliability.py prune and by the extension itself when a file crosses max_bytes_per_file.

state.$comment: The minimum needed to stop duplicate execution and false completion: which calls succeeded, in which generation, with what verification evidence. No prompts, no file bodies.

errors.$comment: Ordered: the first pattern that matches wins, so the specific codes come before the generic ones. Patterns are matched case-insensitively against the tool's error text.

REPEATED_TOOL_CALL.next_action: Do not repeat this call. Inspect the parent directory, verify the active project, search for the name, or change the arguments.

TOOL_CYCLE_DETECTED.next_action: Two calls are alternating without progress. Stop both, re-read the last error, and change strategy - a different tool or a different argument.

DUPLICATE_SUCCESS.next_action: This exact call already succeeded in the current state. Read the earlier result or move to the next step.

NO_PROGRESS.next_action: Stop inspecting. Nothing has been written yet: create the first file with `write` (a small one, then extend it with `edit`). Further reads will be refused until something is on disk.

FILE_NOT_FOUND.next_action: List the parent directory or search for the filename; do not retry this path unchanged.

PATH_OUTSIDE_SANDBOX.next_action: Write inside the repository (and inside the active project when there is one). Use an absolute path only when the repository itself is the target.

PERMISSION_DENIED.next_action: Report the permission boundary and ask for an authorized alternative; repeating the same call will fail identically.

INVALID_ARGUMENT.next_action: Correct the arguments against the tool schema. Do not resend the same payload.

TIMEOUT.next_action: Check whether the server is healthy before retrying; retry once only if the operation is idempotent.

SERVER_UNAVAILABLE.next_action: The MCP server or model endpoint is down. Start or restart it, then retry at most once.

OUTPUT_TOO_LARGE.next_action: Reduce the payload: ranged read, narrower grep, or split the write into a first chunk plus edits.

VALIDATION_FAILED.next_action: Read the validator's actual message and patch the cause; do not resend the same code.

WRITE_NOT_VERIFIED.next_action: The tool claimed success but the file on disk did not change. Re-read the file and retry the write with correct content.

UNKNOWN.next_action: Read the error text and change something before calling again.
